citation: Siqi Gu; Quanjun Zhang; Kecheng Li; Chunrong Fang; Fangyuan Tian; Liuchuan Zhu; Jianyi Zhou; Zhenyu Chen (2024). TestART: Improving LLM-based Unit Testing via Co-evolution of Automated Generation and Repair Iteration. https://arxiv.org/html/2408.03095v6
dataset: Defects4J: 8,192 focal methods / 5 Java projects; HITS: 885; industrial set: 668
setting: JUnit 4 / JDK 1.8; rule-based repairs + iterative LLM repair + coverage-guided prompting; repeated experiments
metric: Passing rate; compilation/runtime error rates; coverage. Đơn vị: focal method với generated tests.
main_result: Table 2: TestART passing 78.55%; ChatGPT-3.5 49.91%; GPT-4 59.75%; ChatUniTest 60.05%.
code_available: Reported public artifact: https://github.com/sikygu/TestART (chưa chạy tái lập)
limitations: Nhiều vòng repair và tăng coverage; không HumanEval/Gemini/human paired baseline. Coverage trên tests đã qua kiểm tra, không thay thế tỷ lệ compile-and-run trên toàn bộ bài.
rq_relevance: CORE: compiler-feedback repair, nguyên nhân lỗi và cách tách pass/compile; không phải bằng chứng cho đúng protocol một vòng sửa của nhóm.

citation: Nadia Alshahwan; Jubin Chheda; Anastasia Finogenova; Beliz Gokkaya; Mark Harman; Inna Harper; Alexandru Marginean; Shubho Sengupta; Eddy Wang (2024). Automated Unit Test Improvement using Large Language Models at Meta. https://arxiv.org/html/2402.09171v1
dataset: Kotlin unit-test classes for Instagram Reels and Stories at Meta
setting: Improve existing human-written test classes; generate candidates; build/reliability/coverage filters
metric: Build success; reliable pass; coverage improvement. Section 3.1: test classes with at least one qualifying new test.
main_result: 75% classes contain >=1 new test that builds; 57% contain >=1 that builds and passes reliably; 25% contain >=1 that also improves line coverage.
code_available: No public replication code verified; proprietary products and internal models
limitations: Abstract/result wording differs in aggregation; Section 3.1 is class-level at-least-one. Kotlin; internal data/models; no fresh HumanEval JUnit generation or paired human success rate.
rq_relevance: CORE: staged validation and separate build/pass outcomes; only methodological support for the group setting.

citation: Chandan Kumar; Usha Sri Ponaka; Pula V. Lakshmi Narasimha Naidu; Pyatlo Bhuvaneswari; Mukesh Prasad; Sunil Kumar Singh (2025). AI-Powered Unit Test Generation via Multi-LLM Chaining: A Case Study With GPT-4o, Gemini, and Claude-3.5. https://doi.org/10.1109/ACCESS.2025.3637221
tool_llm: GPT-4o; Gemini 2.0 Flash; Claude 3.5 Sonnet; Gemini -> GPT-4o / Claude chaining
dataset: HumanEval Java conversion, described as 164 tasks; no frozen 30-task list matching the group
setting: Single-model and multi-model chains; structured prompts; invalid-output retry and coverage-driven iterations; August 2025 model calls
metric: Compilation errors / all generated test cases; runtime failures / all generated test cases; line/branch coverage; mutation score
main_result: Table 2: Gemini compilation errors 13/3,077 (0.42%); GPT-4o 18/2,454 (0.73%). Table 3: runtime failures Gemini 301/3,077 (9.78%); GPT-4o 375/2,454 (15.28%).
limitations: Counts are generated test cases, not 30 problem-level suites. Runtime denominators are total generated tests; overlap/conditional execution not established. No paired human baseline, one-repair control or task-category comparison. Cannot derive the group joint success rate by subtracting both error rates.
rq_relevance: CORE / first priority: same HumanEval Java and GPT/Gemini family; motivates compile/runtime comparison but does not answer the exact paired RQ.

citation: Michael Konstantinou; Renzo Degiovanni; Jie M. Zhang; Mark Harman; Mike Papadakis (2025). YATE: The Role of Test Repair in LLM-Based Unit Test Generation. https://arxiv.org/html/2507.18316v1
tool_llm: YATE; GPT-4o-mini primary; robustness with GPT-4.1 / DeepSeek-V3 / Codestral
setting: JUnit 5; JDK 8/11/17 by project; static repairs + LLM repair + test augmentation; LLM-Plain baseline
metric: Compilation and passing rates in class-level and method-level generation configurations; branch coverage/mutation
main_result: Class-level configuration: LLM-Plain compile 2,865/3,232=88.64%, pass 1,633/3,232=50.53%; YATE compile 4,681/4,948=94.60%, pass 4,462/4,948=90.18%.
limitations: Different generated-test counts across approaches; not paired HumanEval problems. Multiple repair rounds (including oracle fixes) and augmentation; coverage evaluated after validation. No Gemini/human paired baseline.
rq_relevance: CORE: shows repair effects and explicit denominators; extract repair design, do not import rates into the one-repair group experiment.

citation: Jiacheng Xu; Wentao Zhang; Zhiyi Lyu; Fuxiang Zhang; Chaojie Wang; Yang Liu; Bo An (2026). Two-Stage Reinforcement Learning for Sound and Adversarial Test Generation in Code LLMs. https://arxiv.org/html/2609.03955v1
dataset: TACO: 6,318 curated training tasks / 1,000 validation tasks; LiveCodeBench evaluation
setting: Two-stage RL for a Python test generator; reference-checked soundness then adversarial counterexamples
metric: Test soundness/counterexamples; downstream solver pass@1 and best-of-N are program outcomes
main_result: Reports improvement in sound/adversarial test generation and downstream code selection. Solver pass@1 is not generated-test compilation/execution success.
code_available: Repository link reported in paper Appendix A.2; artifact execution not verified
limitations: Python algorithmic tasks; trained small models; no Java/GPT/Gemini or compiler-feedback one-repair protocol. Do not relabel solver pass@1 as test pass rate.
rq_relevance: SUPPORTING: reference validation and test-oracle correctness; contextual evidence only.

citation: Yunhao Liang; Chengguang Gan; Ruixuan Ying; Hanjun Wei; Zhe Cui; Shiwen Ni (2026). Auditing and Decomposing Feedback-Driven Evolution in LLM Test Generation under the Oracle Problem. https://arxiv.org/html/2608.19626v1
dataset: Algorithmic tasks: 142 development, 114 external and 138 held-out audit tasks
setting: Python/JSONL tests; cross-fitted oracle panel; placebo feedback; budget-matched resampling; three seeds
metric: Oracle-conditioned test gain; audit-panel gain; resampling vs mutation
main_result: Single-oracle evaluation inflates apparent gains by 9.46-14.85 percentage points; budget-matched resampling exceeds mutation by 6.01-18.83 points in the reported audits.
limitations: Python task/input-output evaluation; no JUnit compilation or target models. Audit metrics are not overall build/run rates; recent preprint.
rq_relevance: SUPPORTING: avoid favorable oracle/selection bias; independent validation and matched feedback budgets.

citation: Tasmim Rashid; Muhammad Zubair Malik (2026). LM2Alloy: Investigating LLM-Generated Formal Specifications for Automated Test Derivation in Production Software. https://arxiv.org/html/2607.18555v1
tool_llm: GPT-4o web interface; Alloy Analyzer; pytest
dataset: Two Python production libraries: Flipper and Cerberus
setting: Manually select code/docs context; LLM -> Alloy specification -> derived tests; three fresh sessions per prompt
metric: Specification validity; executable derived tests; branch coverage / detected behavioral errors
main_result: Reports valid specifications and executable derived tests without manual correction; finds behavior missed by direct LLM tests. No aggregate JUnit compile/pass numerator and denominator.
code_available: Subject repositories linked; separate replication package not verified
limitations: Two Python case studies; web interface and selected context; no target Java models/one-repair experiment. Qualitative executability statement cannot yield a 30-task rate.
rq_relevance: SUPPORTING: structured specifications and oracle correctness; indirect evidence for prompting/validation.

citation: Tiancheng Ma; Nasir U. Eisty (2026). From Business Requirements to Test Assertions: Evaluating LLM-Generated Oracles on Real Bugs. https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10277v1
dataset: 10 Defects4J Lang bugs (1 and 3-11); Java test oracles
setting: Requirements/SUT/manual oracle comparison; five LLMs; pilot evaluation
metric: Accuracy / precision / recall / F1 of generated oracles; correlation with requirement completeness
main_result: Performance varies across bugs/models. Table 3 uses 9 observations for Mistral because one generated oracle does not compile; other models use 10. Correlation CIs include zero.
limitations: Small pilot; no GPT/Gemini; assertion/oracle generation differs from full suite. Noncompiling output excluded from some metrics: group must retain such cases in its all-problem failure denominator.
rq_relevance: SUPPORTING: assertion validity and denominator/selection bias; no direct compile-and-run success comparison.

citation: Juby George (2026). Large Language Models for Automated Software Test Generation. https://doi.org/10.63090/IJITRS/3139.3209.0022
tool_llm: LLM-Test; GPT-4 primary per methods; zero-shot baseline ambiguously also labeled Codex
dataset: Apache Commons CLI; Gson; JFreeChart; FastJSON
setting: Context/coverage/mutation feedback; up to 10 refinement rounds; five repetitions
metric: Compilation rate; branch coverage; mutation score; detected bugs
main_result: Table 2 reports compile 94.1% LLM-Test vs 87.6% few-shot GPT-4 and 82.3% zero-shot GPT-4; branch coverage 81.5% for LLM-Test. Exact compilation numerator/denominator not reported.
code_available: No replication code/raw-data link verified in full text
limitations: LOW reporting confidence: unspecified model snapshot/project versions and compile denominator; baseline GPT-4/Codex inconsistency. Ten rounds differ from one repair. Do not quantitatively pool these values or use as sole support for RQ.
rq_relevance: SUPPORTING / LOW_CONFIDENCE: compiler/feedback context only; not core quantitative evidence.

citation: Zhiqiang Yuan; Yiling Lou; Mingwei Liu; Shiji Ding; Kaixin Wang; Yixuan Chen; Xin Peng (2024). No More Manual Tests? Evaluating and Improving ChatGPT for Unit Test Generation. https://arxiv.org/html/2305.04207v3
database: Supplementary citation/title discovery + arXiv full-text verification
dataset: 1,000 Java focal methods from 185 projects; additional 100 focal methods for ChatTester
setting: Basic context prompt; compile and execute generated tests; manually classify errors; iterative context enrichment and feedback repair
metric: Generated-test compilation rate and successful execution rate; readability/usability; coverage
main_result: Table 2: ChatGPT compiles 42.1% and passes 24.8% of 1,000 generated tests; EvoSuite 97.6% and 91.4%. Common compile issues include symbols/types/access; execution includes assertion failures.
code_available: Reported artifact: https://github.com/FudanSELab/ChatTester (chưa chạy tái lập)
limitations: ChatTester repair is iterative, not one compiler repair. No Gemini/HumanEval. Human evaluation concerns passing-test readability/usability, not a paired human compile/pass baseline; sample differs for ChatTester.
rq_relevance: CORE / high priority: metric definitions, compiler/runtime failure taxonomy and feedback repair; no direct evidence on the group exact task categories.

citation: Yinghao Chen; Zehao Hu; Chen Zhi; Junxiao Han; Shuiguang Deng; Jianwei Yin (2024). ChatUniTest: A Framework for LLM-Based Test Generation. https://arxiv.org/html/2305.04764v2
database: Supplementary citation/title discovery + arXiv full-text verification
dataset: 4 Java projects (Commons CLI, Commons CSV, ecommerce, Binance); 264 sampled focal methods out of 835
setting: Adaptive context; syntax/compile/runtime validation; rule-based and LLM repair; default one generation with up to five repair attempts per round
metric: Line coverage; validation/repair architecture; no aggregate compile/pass rate table
main_result: Overall line coverage 59.6% vs TestSpark 42.1% and EvoSuite 38.2%; full text describes syntax, compilation and execution validation.
limitations: Coverage differs from compilation/execution success; no HumanEval/Gemini/human paired baseline; multiple repairs. Demo-scale study.
rq_relevance: METHOD SUPPORT: structured context and compiler/runtime validators; do not cite coverage as pass rate.
